thread:
marie: FYI — ACMEHealth just asked for a pilot that combines batching/caching + automated quantization suggestions, plus eval-triggered alerts when quality drops for clinical prompts. They want a short timeline (6 weeks). Can we scope a realistic pilot?

sam: 6 weeks is tight but maybe doable if we limit to 2 models and 1 integration pattern (sync request path). Need to confirm infra for quant experimentation though.

leo: Agree with Sam. Also need to define the evaluation signals: what constitutes a quality regression for them? Clinical prompts might need domain-specific metrics (F1 on entity extraction, hallucination rate).

marie: Good call. ACME suggested three acceptance checks: 1) <5% degradation in domain qa metrics vs baseline, 2) end-to-end p95 latency <= 600ms for their typical load, 3) clear rollback path if eval-alert fires.

aisha: For the quantization part, we can ship an advisor that recommends 8-bit vs 4-bit based on token distribution and eval loss delta. But we should gate 4-bit recommendations behind an eval bucket.

joni: Ops note — we need to be careful with caching KV across tenants. For private deployments it's fine, hosted will need tenant-aware cache keys and TTL policies. Also telemetry for cache hit/miss + per-route latency.

sam: Proposal: Pilot lanes = { lane A: batch+caching + 8-bit recommendations; lane B: batch+caching + conservative 4-bit candidate but disabled by default; lane C: eval-alerts + auto-tagging for rollback }. Start with Lane A + eval-alert infra.

marie: I like lanes. For coms: we should give ACME a 2-week alpha with Lane A only, then opt-in to Lane B for risk-based testing. Lane C should be passive alerts for first 2 weeks.

leo: Need concrete metrics to feed eval-alerts. Suggest: per-prompt embedding cosine drift, token-level perplexity shift, and a small human-annotated concordance set (50 queries). Alert thresholds: cosine drop > 0.08 or perplexity increase > 10%.

aisha: We'll need a lightweight eval harness in the console and a webhook to notify ACME -> runbook trigger. I can prototype a UI card and a webhook payload shape in 3 days.

marie: Ok. Can someone draft minimal acceptance criteria and rollout steps for legal/Sales? I want this in the pilot doc by EOD Friday.

sam: I'll draft the technical acceptance checklist: model variants, quant profiles, batching config, cache key scheme, SLI defs (p95 latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens).

joni: I'll add the ops checklist: tenant-aware caching, telemetry retention, canary rollout plan, audit logs, and an emergency kill switch that forces fallback to full-precision model.

leo: Quick note on instrumentation: include per-quantization-per-model delta metrics so we can attribute quality regressions to quant choices. Without that it's hard to blame anything.

marie: Great. If we can get a short tech spec + roll-out plan by Friday and a prototype webhook/UI by next Wed, I'll push the pilot contract to ACME. I'll also prepare a prioritized backlog of follow-ups (A/B quant experiments, per-route econ suggestions).

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/optimize-pilot-harness -> staging at 2026-03-23T15:04:00Z :rocket:

aisha: ack. I'll watch the staging run and drop screenshots in the doc.

marie: Thanks all — keeping scope tight is critical here. We can expand to multi-model and mobile batching after we have baseline signals. :thumbsup:
